title: How Trolley Problems Work
summary: Josh Clark and Chris Pallette discuss the trolley problem, a philosophical thought experiment about whether to sacrifice one life to save several. They walk through the lever (switch) version, where pulling the switch kills one man on a side track instead of five or fifteen on the trolley, and the footbridge-style version, where one large man must be pushed onto the tracks to stop the trolley. They discuss the difference between allowing a death and actively causing one, how most people would pull the lever but not push the man, the utilitarian view, and how such reasoning relates to rules like organ transplant policy. The episode is a promotional-style discussion tied to a HowStuffWorks article on the topic.
topics: sacrificing one life to save many

segments.title: Opening and introduction
segments.summary: Brief sponsor line and show introduction; Josh introduces the topic of the trolley problem as an article he wrote.

segments.title: The trolley problem: lever and footbridge scenarios
segments.summary: Josh describes the basic trolley dilemma: a runaway trolley will kill five people, and a switch could divert it onto a track where one man is standing. He then describes the second version, with no switch, where a large person must be pushed onto the tracks to stop the trolley.

segments.title: Allowing death versus actively killing
segments.summary: Chris and Josh discuss whether they would pull the lever or push the man. They note that the problem, first posed in the 1960s, distinguishes allowing a death from actively causing one, and that pulling the lever is easier to accept than pushing someone.

segments.title: Utilitarianism and real-world rules
segments.summary: Josh says most people would pull the lever but not push the man, and explains this in terms of utilitarianism. He links the reasoning to societal rules, using an example about organ transplants, and closes with a promotion for the HowStuffWorks article.
